seoTitle: Aside — Free AI Web Translator & Reading Assistant
seoDescription: Free, open-source Chrome extension for AI bilingual page translation, explanations, Q&A and saved passages. Connect your own cloud or local models.
productType: AI reading assistant · Open-source Chrome extension
lead: Use AI to translate pages, explain difficult passages, pull out key points, and answer questions about what you’re reading. Translations stay beside the original, so you can keep reading without switching to a separate chat window.
installNote: For Chrome 120+. No sign-up, free to use. Connect to your choice of cloud or local models (model services may charge fees).
featuresIntro: Read the translation without losing the original.
inlineText: Translations sit below the original paragraphs, so both languages stay in view.
scrollText: Translate the visible area first. More passages are processed as you scroll or the page changes.
restoreText: Restore the page whenever you want. Your place in the text stays familiar.
qaText: Select a passage to translate or explain it in a floating panel. Ask a follow-up question with Quick Q&A, using the selection or the page as context.
qaStandalone: Clear the quote when you want to ask something on its own.
collectionText: Save a useful result with the original text and its source. Search your collection, revisit a passage, and pick up the thought again.
dailyText: Today’s thought offers a short daily reflection, optionally inspired by your collection.
darkText: A built-in {darkReader} engine brings dark mode to websites for reading in dim light. Enable it per site, or follow your system.
appearanceText: Adjust result colors, type size, and spacing to suit the way you read.
actionsText: Explain a concept, interpret a classical text, or extract the key points. Add optional requirements to built-in actions, or create and try an action of your own.
languagesText: Choose from 15 interface languages. Set the output language separately for each action.
tabsText: Use {tabsShortcut} to switch between the last two tabs in your window. On macOS, use Option. Customize shortcuts in Chrome.
modelsText: Connect a service you already use with its endpoint and API key. Aside supports these interfaces:
localModelsText: Compatible local model endpoints on localhost are supported too.
directText: Requests go directly to your chosen model service, with no Aside relay server or analytics. Collections and request history are stored in your browser.
freeAnswer: Aside is free and open source under the MIT license. AI features require your own model access. Your provider may charge for requests; no model subscription or API credit is included.
modelsAnswer: Choose a provider that supports one of the four interfaces listed above. In Model connections, enter its service address and API key, test the connection, then select a model. You can keep multiple connections and choose one for each action.
localAnswer: Yes, with a local service that exposes a compatible API, such as {ollamaLink}. Select OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and use its localhost address. The service and model must support the requests you use. Local HTTP connections are limited to localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1].
dataAnswer: Translation and other AI features send the required content directly to your chosen model service. Once page translation is started, scrolling can send more passages. With a model configured, Today’s thought can generate on the first Collection visit each day and optionally reference saved passages; hide it to stop automatic generation. The provider’s own data policy applies. {privacyLink}
installIntro: Get Aside from the Chrome Web Store, then connect your preferred model to start reading.
downloadText: Get the extension ZIP using the button below. Choose the packaged extension, not GitHub’s “Source code” download.
unzipText: Extract the ZIP into a folder you will keep. Chrome loads the extension from that folder.
loadText: Open {extensions}, enable {developerMode}, choose {loadUnpacked}, and select the extracted folder.
afterInstall: Then open Aside’s Settings and add a model connection. Return to a regular web page to start translating or asking questions.
footerText: A little help, beside your reading.
heroTitle: Read with clarity. Think more deeply.
installTitle: Start with a page worth reading.
localQuestion: Can I use a local model?
dataQuestion: Where does my reading data go?
translationCaption: Original and translation, together on the page.
screenshotCaption: Real extension interface with example content. Select an image to enlarge it.
translationAlt: French paragraphs with English translations directly below them, rendered by Aside.
qaAlt: A selected passage about explaining and justifying beliefs, with Aside clarifying the distinction.
collectionAlt: Aside’s Collection page with a daily reflection and three saved passages.
darkAlt: An article in dark mode with Aside’s floating menu open.
syncAvailability: Coming in the next Chrome Web Store update
syncText: Optionally sync model connections, reading actions, and reflection settings through Chrome. Your configuration is encrypted with a passphrase you choose before it leaves your device.
syncJoinText: Sign in to the same Chrome account with sync enabled, then join in Aside with the same passphrase. Allow access to model services on each device.
syncLocalText: Collections, generated thoughts, request history, and cached results do not sync. Language and appearance preferences stay local too.
